title: Best Screen Recording Software for Mac in 2026
summary: Compare the best screen recorders for Mac in 2026, including QuickTime, Screen Studio, CleanShot X, and Clueso for polished training videos.
body_markdown:
Mac users looking for a screen recorder run into two different jobs that get lumped into one search. Some need to capture a quick clip and share it in the next five minutes. Others need to turn that recording into a polished, branded training or product video without spending hours in an editor. This guide compares the best screen recording software for Mac across both jobs, from the free tool already built into macOS to the AI-powered platforms that write a script and voiceover for you.


## Comparing the best screen recorders for Mac at a glance


QuickTime Player, Screen Studio, CleanShot X, and Loom work best when fast capture and sharing are the priority. Clueso is better suited to producing finished training videos with scripts, narration, and branding.

## QuickTime Player: the free Mac screen recorder you already have


QuickTime Player suits one-off internal captures where speed matters more than presentation. Apple includes it with macOS, so you can record a full screen or selected area without installing another app. QuickTime Player adds no watermark or preset recording limit, which makes it useful for bug reports, quick walkthroughs, and informal updates.


QuickTime Player can record microphone input, but its system-audio options vary by macOS version and recording method. If the required audio source is unavailable, capturing sound from an app may require a compatible virtual audio driver and changes to the Mac's audio routing. The additional setup makes QuickTime Player less convenient for tutorials that need software sounds or meeting audio.


QuickTime also leaves most production work to you. The app lacks automatic zooms, script generation, voiceovers, branding controls, and a meaningful editing workflow. You will need separate software to turn a raw capture into a consistent training video.


Choose QuickTime when you need a free recording for a short-lived bug report, walkthrough, or internal update. Repeatable onboarding, customer education, and branded product tutorials usually call for screen recording software for Mac that handles the work after capture.


## Screen Studio: automatic zooms for Mac creators


Screen Studio suits solo Mac creators who want polished motion without editing on a timeline. The app tracks clicks, adds automatic zooms, and smooths cursor movement after capture. You can also trim footage, adjust its speed, add basic branding, and export it as MP4 or GIF.


Screen Studio centers on polishing the original capture rather than producing a separate script, AI narration, and written SOP. Check the current version before relying on any specific AI or transcript-editing capability, since those features can change between releases.


Screen Studio runs on macOS and centers its workflow on polishing individual screen recordings. That focus works well for a creator making product demos or tutorials on a Mac. Teams producing repeatable onboarding content may need a broader workflow for script creation, narration, branding, and written SOPs.


## CleanShot X: the Mac-native toolkit for screenshots and recordings


CleanShot X fits developers and support staff who share bug reports, technical explanations, and quick internal documentation. Its Mac-native toolkit combines screen recording with scrolling capture, on-device text recognition, annotation, and redaction. You can capture a long webpage, hide sensitive details, copy text from the image, and share the result without moving between several apps.


CleanShot X also records system audio, microphone audio, webcam video, clicks, and keyboard shortcuts. Automatic smart zooms guide attention during playback, while Studio Mode lets you trim mistakes and fine-tune zooms before exporting an MP4 or GIF. Those controls provide more polish than QuickTime Player while keeping the editing process relatively light.


CleanShot X requires more manual work when you use it to produce recurring training videos. Studio Mode still requires you to review and edit each recording, and CleanShot X does not generate a script or AI voiceover. If you need recurring branded onboarding or product videos, Clueso can generate the script, voiceover, and supporting SOP after capture. CleanShot X remains the stronger choice when fast capture, annotation, OCR, and redaction matter more than a finished narrated video.


## Loom: fast async screen recording for Mac, built for sharing


Loom suits people who want to record their screen and share the result through a link with minimal setup. The app supports Mac, Windows, and browser-based recording, which suits groups working across operating systems. Its workflow emphasizes recording, transcription, and link sharing rather than detailed timeline editing.


Loom's recording limits, playback quality, AI features, and prices vary by plan. Check Loom's current plan details before choosing it for long recordings, high-resolution exports, transcript-based editing, or AI-generated documentation.


Loom's AI features help people process and share an existing recording, including through summaries or written documentation on eligible plans. Clueso is oriented toward producing a branded training asset with a revised script, generated narration, visual editing, and a matching SOP. Loom remains better suited to quick updates and link-based collaboration.


## Clueso: turning Mac screen recordings into polished training videos with AI


[Clueso](https://www.clueso.io/) fits teams that need to turn a raw Mac screen recording into a finished training or product video. You can begin with a screen recording instead of writing a script before capture. Clueso uses AI to revise the script and generate a voiceover. It also applies visual edits without requiring you to work on a traditional editing timeline.


QuickTime Player and CleanShot X emphasize capture, while Loom emphasizes capture and link-based sharing. Screen Studio adds automatic zooms and cursor effects for a more polished recording. Clueso handles the production work that follows capture, which makes it better suited to repeatable customer education, employee onboarding, and product demonstrations.


Clueso also generates an SOP from the recording, so one capture can produce both video and written instructions. Reusable Clueprints apply the same branding and structure across multiple videos. AI-written scripts and generated voiceovers reduce the need to rewrite and rerecord narration whenever the product changes.


Clueso makes the most sense when speed means reducing post-production work rather than starting the recording a few seconds faster. A solo user sharing a bug report will usually find QuickTime, CleanShot, or Loom simpler. Clueso better serves people building a branded training library because it combines script revision, voiceover generation, visual editing, and SOP creation in one workflow.


Compare Clueso with traditional timeline editors in Clueso's[Camtasia alternatives comparison](https://www.clueso.io/compare/camtasia-alternatives) . You can also use Clueso's AI Screen Recorder to capture a Mac workflow directly.


## Which screen recording software for Mac should you choose?


Choose QuickTime Player when you need a free, one-off recording for a bug report or basic walkthrough. CleanShot X suits developers and support staff who also need screenshots, annotations, redaction, and quick sharing.


Choose Screen Studio if you are a solo creator who wants polished cursor movement and automatic zooms with little editing. Its Mac-only workflow works well for product demos, but it does not generate scripts or voiceovers.


Choose Loom if you need to record and share an update across Mac and Windows without producing a fully narrated training video.


Choose Clueso when you need repeatable, branded training or onboarding content. Clueso turns a raw screen recording into a polished video with an enhanced script, AI voiceover, captions, and a matching SOP. That workflow reduces the manual production work required across a growing video library.


## FAQs


**Does Mac have a built-in screen recorder?** Yes. QuickTime Player and the Shift-Command-5 screenshot toolbar provide free, built-in screen recording for basic captures.


**Can you record system audio on Mac for free?** Available system-audio options depend on the macOS version and recording method. If QuickTime Player does not offer the required audio source, a compatible virtual audio driver can route system sound into the recording, although setup requires changing the Mac's audio routing. CleanShot X also supports system-audio capture within its recording workflow.


**What is the best screen recorder for Mac tutorials and training videos?** Screen Studio suits polished solo tutorials, while CleanShot X suits quick annotated walkthroughs. Clueso fits recurring training programs that need branded videos with revised scripts, AI voiceovers, and matching SOPs.


**Does Clueso replace a separate screen recorder?** Yes. Clueso includes screen capture, so you can record and produce the finished video in one workflow. You can also import an existing Mac recording when QuickTime, CleanShot X, or another recorder better suits the capture step.
